The Toronto Raptors couldn't have asked for a much better start to the 2026-27 season after dismantling the Chicago Bulls 135-92, the largest home opener win in franchise history. Toronto heads to Washington on Friday looking to carry that momentum against a Wizards team that also opened its season with a win.
 Toronto's return to the court was highlighted by the reunion with Kawhi Leonard, who scored 23 points in his first regular-season game back with the Raptors. Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley also recorded 23 points apiece, while RJ Barrett added 20.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Raptors established control immediately, scoring 43 points in the first quarter and forcing 27 turnovers. Their defensive pressure and balanced scoring proved too much for Chicago, although Toronto will want to see whether it can maintain that intensity against stronger opposition
 TORONTO, CANADA – OCTOBER 21: Kawhi Leonard #2 of the Toronto Raptors drives against Matas Buzelis #14 of the Chicago Bulls in the first half of their NBA game at Scotiabank Arena on October 21, 2026 in Toronto, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Cole Burston/Getty Images) | Getty Images
 Washington also began its campaign with an impressive performance, defeating the Milwaukee Bucks 128-116. Anthony Davis led the way with 34 points and 12 rebounds, while Trae Young contributed 20 points and 13 assists. The Wizards overcame a slow start with a decisive fourth-quarter run to secure the victory.
 Players to watch
 Kawhi Leonard will be one to watch after a successful first game in his return to Toronto's lineup. His two-way presence gives the Raptors another scoring option, while Scottie Barnes' ability to contribute as a scorer, rebounder and playmaker will be crucial to Toronto's success.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While the majority of the starting five played well, I would like to see more production from the bench, as I expect them to play a bigger role in this game against the Wizards.
 For Washington, Anthony Davis presents the biggest matchup concern after his performance in the season opener. His interior scoring and rim protection could challenge Toronto on both ends of the floor, while Trae Young's playmaking will be key to the Wizards' offence.
 Young's connection with Davis could create problems for the Raptors if they allow the duo to dictate the pace.
 A player that I was excited to watch is first overall pick, AJ Dybantsa, though he has been ruled out for Friday's contest.

 Keys to the game
 The biggest question is whether Toronto can force turnovers and generate easy points again. The Raptors thrived on defensive pressure against Chicago, but Washington's combination of Young's passing and Davis' finishing presents a different challenge.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The battle inside will also be important. Toronto must find a way to limit Davis without overcommitting defensively and leaving Washington's perimeter players open.
 Meanwhile, the Raptors' ball movement and ability to get contributions from multiple scorers should help determine whether they can control the game.
 Washington will also be looking to improve its perimeter shooting after struggling from three-point range against Milwaukee. If the Wizards find their touch from deep, they could make this a much closer contest.
 Prediction
 Toronto has the momentum and demonstrated how dangerous its offence can be when Barnes, Quickley, Barrett and Leonard contribute together. However, Davis and Young give Washington a formidable duo that should make things more difficult for the Raptors.
 TORONTO, ON- OCTOBER 21 – Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard #2 of the Toronto Raptors share a laugh on the bench as the Toronto Raptors play the Chicago Bulls in their season opener at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto. October 21, 2026. Steve Russell/Toronto Star (Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images) | Toronto Star via Getty Images
 Prediction: Raptors 114, Wizards 108. 
 Toronto's depth and defensive pressure should be enough to secure a second straight win, but I would expect this to be a much closer matchup.
